problems.title: A sum-to-product quotient
problems.question: Simplify(sinα+sinβ)/(cosα+cosβ).
problems.idea: Use a trigonometric identity or a projection formula, with the original restrictions.
formulas: The numerator is 2sin((α+β)/2)cos((α−β)/2); the denominator is 2cos((α+β)/2)cos((α−β)/2).
steps: Cancel the common factor where the original denominator is nonzero. The result is tan((α+β)/2).

problems.title: Three equally spaced trigonometric arguments
problems.question: Simplify(sinα+sin3α+sin5α)/(cosα+cos3α+cos5α).
problems.idea: Use a trigonometric identity or a projection formula, with the original restrictions.
formulas: Pair the outside terms:sinα+sin5α=2sin3αcos2α, andcosα+cos5α=2cos3αcos2α.
steps: The numerator and denominator share1+2cos2α. Cancelling on the original domain givestan3α.

problems.title: Compare least periods
problems.question: Which pair amonga=3tan4x+1, b=5|cot8x|+1, c=cos4x+2, d=2|sin4x|+1 have the same least positive period?
problems.idea: Use a trigonometric identity or a projection formula, with the original restrictions.
formulas: The least periods are π/4,π/8,π/2,π/4, respectively.
steps: Thus a and d share the periodπ/4. Absolute sine halves the ordinary sine period; absolute cotangent keeps its periodπ.

problems.title: Surface area of a unit-edge hexagonal prism
problems.question: All 18 edges of a regular hexagonal prism are 1. Find total surface are a.
problems.idea: Use a trigonometric identity or a projection formula, with the original restrictions.
formulas: Each base are a is 6·√3/4=3√3/2; the lateral are a is perimeter×height=6.

problems.title: Surface area under uniform scaling
problems.question: Every edge of a rectangular box decreases10%. By what percentage does total are a decrease?
problems.idea: Use a trigonometric identity or a projection formula, with the original restrictions.
formulas: Lengths scale by 0.9, so areas scale by 0.9²=0.81.
steps: The decrease is 1−0.81=0.19, or 19%.

problems.title: Compare four function ranges
problems.question: For the four functions in Problem3, which pair have the same range?
problems.idea: Use a trigonometric identity or a projection formula, with the original restrictions.
formulas: Tangent has rangeℝ,|cot| has[0,∞), coshas[−1,1],|sin|has[0,1].
steps: After scaling and shifting, the ranges areℝ,[1,∞),[1,3],[1,3]. Thusc and d agree.

problems.title: A missing minus sign in a standard identity
problems.question: Which printed product-to-sum or sum-to-product formula is false?
problems.idea: Use a trigonometric identity or a projection formula, with the original restrictions.
formulas: The correct formula iscosα−cosβ=−2sin((α+β)/2)sin((α−β)/2).
steps: The last displayed option has a plus sign instead. For exampleα=π,β=0 gives left side −2 and its proposed right side 2.
problems.answer: The final cosine-difference formula is false.

problems.title: Reduce a triple-angle quotient
problems.question: Evaluate44(cosα−cos3α)/[sin2α·sin3α], givencos²α=0.8.
problems.idea: Use a trigonometric identity or a projection formula, with the original restrictions.
formulas: cosα−cos3α=2sin2αsinα; sin3α=sinα(3−4sin²α).
steps: On the original domain, the quotient becomes88/(3−4sin²α).
Since sin²α=0.2, the value is 88/(3−0.8)=40.

problems.title: Height of a median midpoint
problems.question: Triangle vertices are distances5,12,7 from a plane that does not cross the triangle. Find the distance of the midpoint of median BM.
problems.idea: Use a trigonometric identity or a projection formula, with the original restrictions.
formulas: Signed distance to a plane is affine, and all three distances have the same sign.
steps: The midpoint M of AC is distance(5+7)/2=6. The midpoint of BM is distance(12+6)/2=9.

problems.title: A prism over a bicentric trapezoid
problems.question: A right prism has height 2√5 and trapezoid base lengths 6,10. Interior upper-base points are equidistant from lower-base sides and vertices, respectively. Find its space diagonal.
problems.idea: Use a trigonometric identity or a projection formula, with the original restrictions.
formulas: The base has an incircle and circumcircle, so it is an isosceles tangential trapezoid. Legs=(6+10)/2=8; its altitude is √(8²−2²)=2√15.
steps: The horizontal diagonal component is(6+10)/2=8. Thus a base diagonal squared is 8²+(2√15)²=124.
Add the prism height squared20 to get space-diagonal squared144. Its length is 12.

problems.title: Half-angle square roots with correct signs
problems.question: Simplify√(1+sinα)+√(1−sinα) for 90°<α<180°.
problems.idea: Use a trigonometric identity or a projection formula, with the original restrictions.
formulas: Write1±sinα=(sin(α/2)±cos(α/2))². Here sin(α/2)>cos(α/2)>0.
steps: The roots are sin(α/2)+cos(α/2) and sin(α/2)−cos(α/2).
Their sum is 2sin(α/2).

problems.title: Difference between a tangent product and quotient
problems.question: Compare tan2α·tanα withtan2α/tanα on their common domain.
problems.idea: Use a trigonometric identity or a projection formula, with the original restrictions.
formulas: Putt=tanα. Their difference is[2t/(1−t²)](t−1/t).
steps: This simplifies to −2. Thus the product is 2 less than the quotient.

problems.title: Maximum of a squared linear sine-cosine sum
problems.question: Maximise6sinxcosx+9cos²x+sin²x.
problems.idea: Use a trigonometric identity or a projection formula, with the original restrictions.
formulas: The expression is(sinx+3cosx)². By Cauchy–Schwarz, it is at most(1²+3²)(sin²x+cos²x)=10.
steps: Equality is attainable when(sinx, cosx) is proportional to(1,3).

problems.title: Equal inclined sections with different projected areas
problems.question: Two section planes through a triangle base’s two side midpoints cut a quadrilateral at inclinationα and triangle at inclinationβ. Their section areas are equal. Find the relation.
problems.idea: Use a trigonometric identity or a projection formula, with the original restrictions.
formulas: Their base projections have areas3S/4 and S/4. Orthogonal projection multiplies an are a bycos(inclination).
steps: Equality of section areas gives(3S/4)/cosα=(S/4)/cosβ.
Thuscosα=3cosβ.

problems.title: An octagonal prism’s shortest space diagonal
problems.question: A regular octagonal prism’s shortest space diagonal equals its base’s longest diagonal. Find lateral-edge²/base-edge².
problems.idea: Use a trigonometric identity or a projection formula, with the original restrictions.
formulas: Withbase circumradius R, the shortest base diagonal is √2R, the longest2R, and base edgea=2Rsin(π/8).
steps: The space-diagonal condition givesh²+2R²=4R², soh²=2R².

problems.title: A rational cosine from three rational sines
problems.question: sin2α, sin7α, sin12α are nonzero rational numbers. What follows aboutcos5α?
problems.idea: Use a trigonometric identity or a projection formula, with the original restrictions.
formulas: sin2α+sin12α=2sin7αcos5α.
steps: Thuscos5α=(sin2α+sin12α)/(2sin7α), a ratio of rational numbers with nonzero denominator.
problems.answer: It is necessarily rational; only A is true.

problems.title: Sum of sines in arithmetic progression
problems.question: Evaluatesin10°+sin20°+sin30°+sin40°+sin50°.
problems.idea: Use a trigonometric identity or a projection formula, with the original restrictions.
formulas: For five equally spaced angles, the sum is[sin(5·10°/2)/sin(10°/2)]·sin30°.
steps: Since sin30°=1/2, the result issin25°/(2sin5°).

problems.title: Which function fails the subtraction identity?
problems.question: Which listedf does not satisfyf(x+y)f(x−y)=f(x)²−f(y)²?
problems.idea: Use a trigonometric identity or a projection formula, with the original restrictions.
formulas: Linear functionsf=kx satisfy the difference-of-squares identity, and f=k sinx satisfies sin(x+y)sin(x−y)=sin²x−sin²y.
steps: Forf=cosx, sety=0. The left side iscos²x, the right sidecos²x−1, so they disagree.

problems.title: A perpendicular section of a rhombohedron
problems.question: Every face of a parallelepiped is a side-2 rhombus with acute angle 60°. A plane perpendicular to the lateral edges cuts all four of them. Find section are a.
problems.idea: Use a trigonometric identity or a projection formula, with the original restrictions.
formulas: Project the two base-edge vectorsu, v onto the plane perpendicular to the lateral vectorw. Each projected squared length is 4−2²/4=3.
steps: For a nondegenerate rhombohedron, the projected dot product has absolute value1; the alternative absolute value3 would make the three edges coplanar.
The section is the projected parallelogram, with are a √(3·3−1²)=2√2.

problems.title: A vertex equidistant from four base sides
problems.question: An upper-base vertex is distance 5 from every side of the lower parallelogram base. Base diagonals are 6,8. Find total surface are a.
problems.idea: Use a trigonometric identity or a projection formula, with the original restrictions.
formulas: The vertex’s projection is an interior equidistant point, so the parallelogram base is a rhombus. Its diagonals are perpendicular, are a 24, andside5.
steps: Each of the two adjacent lateral faces has are a base-side 5 times point-to-side-line distance 5, or 25. Opposite faces are congruent, so all four total100.
Add two base areas48 to obtain148.

problems.title: Three graphs remain defined below the sine axis
problems.question: Which listed line meets exactly three graphs:y=sinx, positive-part(sinx),√(sin²x),(√sinx)²?
problems.idea: Use a trigonometric identity or a projection formula, with the original restrictions.
formulas: The first three are defined for all realx. The fourth is defined only where sinx≥0.
steps: Atx=1.2π, sinx<0, so the vertical line meets the first three graphs but not the fourth.
The other listed verticals have positive sine; the listed horizontals meet four, one, orzero graphs.

problems.title: Closest zeros of an even shifted sine
problems.question: Find the least distance between distinct zeros ofsin(|x|−π/5).
problems.idea: Use a trigonometric identity or a projection formula, with the original restrictions.
formulas: Zeros satisfy|x|=π/5+nπ, with n≥0.
steps: On each side, the spacing is π. Across the origin, the closest pair is±π/5, with separation2π/5.

problems.title: Count regions made by three curves in a strip
problems.question: How many regions do y=sinx, y=tanx, y=1 for m inπ/6≤x≤π/3?
problems.idea: Use a trigonometric identity or a projection formula, with the original restrictions.
formulas: Throughout the strip, sinx<1 and sinx<tanx. The tangent graph crossesy=1 once, at π/4.
steps: The sine curve first splits the strip into2 regions. The horizontal line adds1.
The tangent curve is split into two arcs by its one crossing with the horizontal, adding2 more regions. Total=5.

problems.title: All parallelepipeds satisfy a diagonal-square identity
problems.question: For which parallelepipeds does the sum of four space-diagonal squares equal the sum of all twelve edge squares?
problems.idea: Use a trigonometric identity or a projection formula, with the original restrictions.
formulas: Expand|±u±v±w|² for the four diagonal sign patterns; the cross terms cancel.
steps: The diagonal sum is 4(|u|²+|v|²+|w|²). Each edge direction occurs on four edges, so the edge-square sum is identical.

problems.title: Possible cosine between two right-prism diagonals
problems.question: A right parallelepiped has base edges3,5, height 4. Which listed acute-angle cosine can occur between A₁C and B₁D?
problems.idea: Use a trigonometric identity or a projection formula, with the original restrictions.
formulas: Withbase angleφ, the diagonal dot product is 32, and their length product is √(2500−900cos²φ).
steps: A nondegenerate base has|cosφ|<1, so the cosine range is[32/50,32/40)=[0.64,0.8).
Only 0.7 among0.4,0.5,0.6,0.7,0.8,0.9 belongs to that range.
